lead: A common rail stores diesel at high pressure in one pipe and lets an electronic control unit fire each injector when it wants. The high-pressure pump now feeds a rail continuously, so pressure generation is separated from the injection event. Rail pressure and injection timing become independent settings. This gives fine sprays, quiet combustion and low emissions. It is used in cars, buses, trucks and tractors, and in petrol direct-injection engines with a similar rail.
prereq: You need: Chapter 2.2 for what an injection system must do, and Chapter 2.3 for why mechanical pumps tie pressure to engine speed.

sections.h3: The layout: from tank to rail

blocks.text: Start at the tank. A lift pump, usually electric, pushes diesel at a few bar through a filter to the high-pressure pump. The filter matters: the pump and injectors have clearances of a few micrometres, and a particle that size can jam an injector. The high-pressure pump is driven by the engine. It raises fuel to the rail pressure and sends it into the rail. The rail is a thick pipe that acts as an accumulator, so all injectors see the same stored pressure.

A pressure sensor on the rail reports to the electronic control unit (ECU). A pressure control valve, on the pump or on the rail, opens to bleed fuel back to the tank and hold the set pressure. The ECU then commands each injector to open. The injector may use a solenoid or a piezo stack. Some syllabi call this common rail diesel injection.

items: Tank stores diesel at low pressure.
Lift pump sends fuel through the filter.
High-pressure pump raises fuel to rail pressure.
Rail stores the high-pressure fuel for all cylinders.
Pressure sensor and control valve keep rail pressure at the ECU set point.
ECU opens each injector at the calculated time.

sections.h3: Two settings: pressure and open time

blocks.text: Rail pressure is set by the pump output and the pressure control valve. Injection timing is set by when the ECU opens an injector. Engine speed does not force the injection start, as it does with a jerk pump. Rail pressure is typically 1000 to 2000 bar, which is 100 to 200 MPa. The ECU reads speed, load, air mass, coolant temperature and rail pressure, then looks up the pressure and timing for that operating point.

For a fixed nozzle, volume per injection rises with injector open time and with the square root of the pressure difference across the nozzle. Fuel quantity is therefore not set by rail pressure alone. The ECU must know both rail pressure and open time. This is the central trap in exams and in calibration.

The ECU can split one injection into several pulses. A pilot injection is a small early pulse. It starts a mild burn, shortens the ignition delay of the main charge, and lowers the rate of pressure rise, so diesel knock and noise fall. The main injection delivers most of the fuel, and therefore most of the work. A post injection comes late, after the main pulse, and is used mainly for exhaust after-treatment, such as heating the exhaust for a diesel particulate filter. Multiple injections per cycle are common.

sections.h3: What it buys, what it costs

items: High rail pressure gives small droplets and fast mixing, so combustion is cleaner.
Pilot injection lowers combustion noise and the peak pressure rise.
Split injection can lower both nitrogen oxides and soot. Retarded timing lowers nitrogen oxides but tends to increase soot, so the ECU trades one against the other.
Cold start and altitude operation can be recalibrated without changing hardware.
Limits: the high-pressure pump, sensor, control valve and ECU add cost and complexity.
The pump takes engine power, filtration must be fine, and injector deposits can disturb the spray.

blocks.text: The system is flexible but not free. A mechanic needs diagnostic tools, and a weak battery or a bad sensor can stop the engine. The gain is a diesel that is quieter, cleaner and easier to calibrate than a mechanical pump line nozzle system.

spec.title: Common rail layout
spec.aria: A common-rail layout: fuel runs from tank through lift pump and filter to a high-pressure pump, then to a rail and injectors. A rail pressure sensor sends a signal to the ECU. The ECU commands the pressure control valve and injector timing.

examples.question: A four-cylinder four-stroke diesel engine runs at 3000 rpm. Each injector delivers 30 mm³ per injection. Find the fuel flow in L/h.
steps: A four-stroke cylinder fires once every two revolutions. Injections per cylinder per minute = 3000 ÷ 2 = 1500.
examples.check:
rpm = 3000
n_cyl = 4
vol_mm3 = 30
inj_per_cyl_min = rpm / 2
total_inj_min = n_cyl * inj_per_cyl_min
vol_mm3_min = vol_mm3 * total_inj_min
vol_cm3_min = vol_mm3_min / 1000
vol_L_min = vol_cm3_min / 1000
flow_L_h = vol_L_min * 60
print(inj_per_cyl_min)
print(total_inj_min)
print(vol_mm3_min)
print(vol_cm3_min)
print(vol_L_min)
print(flow_L_h)

traps: Saying rail pressure alone sets injection quantity. Quantity depends on rail pressure and injector open time together.
Treating common rail as a petrol-only system. This chapter is diesel common rail; petrol direct injection uses a similar rail but different mixture needs.
Thinking pilot injection adds power. The pilot pulse mainly reduces ignition delay and noise; the main pulse does the work.
Calling post injection a late power pulse only. Its main job is exhaust after-treatment, such as diesel particulate filter regeneration.
Assuming higher rail pressure is always better. It improves spray but raises pump work, nitrogen oxides and wear, so the ECU balances it.

quiz.q: What is stored in the common rail?
quiz.a: High-pressure diesel from the high-pressure pump. The rail is an accumulator that feeds all injectors at the same pressure.

quiz.q: State the typical rail pressure range for a diesel common rail.
quiz.a: About 1000 to 2000 bar, which is 100 to 200 MPa.

quiz.q: Why does a common rail let pressure and injection timing be set independently?
quiz.a: A separate high-pressure pump and rail hold the pressure. The ECU opens each injector when needed. The pump plunger speed does not decide the injection start.
It is a small early pulse. It starts a mild burn, shortens the ignition delay of the main charge, lowers the pressure rise and reduces diesel noise.

quiz.q: A six-cylinder four-stroke engine runs at 3000 rpm with 30 mm³ per injection. Find the fuel flow in L/h.
quiz.a: Injections per cylinder per minute = 3000/2 = 1500. Total = 6 × 1500 = 9000 per minute. Volume = 30 × 9000 = 270000 mm³/min = 270 cm³/min = 0.27 L/min = 16.2 L/h.

quiz.q: Why can a common rail reduce both noise and nitrogen oxides, which often conflict?
quiz.a: Pilot injection cuts noise by starting the burn gently. Multiple injections and retarded timing lower the peak temperature and nitrogen oxides. High pressure improves mixing and limits soot. The ECU chooses the trade-off for each speed and load.

quiz.q: Compare a common rail with a jerk pump on pressure, timing and cost.
quiz.a: A jerk pump makes pressure by plunger motion and times delivery by spill, so pressure and timing move with speed. It is cheap and robust. A common rail uses a separate pump, rail and ECU injectors, so pressure and timing are independent and split injection is possible. It costs more and needs sensors and fine filtration.

beyond: Not for the exam. Modern common-rail diesel systems use piezo injectors and rail pressures above 2000 bar to shape the injection rate. The same rail layout appears in petrol direct injection, where the fuel is gasoline and the injector sits in the cylinder. Search for piezo common rail, injection rate shaping, and diesel particulate filter regeneration by post injection.
